title: State AI laws and changing federal policy

sources.claim: Colorado's 2024 AI Act (SB 24-205) was delayed in 2025 and, on May 14, 2026, repealed and replaced by SB 26-189, with a narrower law set to take effect January 1, 2027; federal litigation over the earlier law was also reported. An example of how quickly AI rules change.

Executive Order 14365 (December 11, 2025) directed federal agencies to challenge some state AI laws and to propose a national framework; an executive order directs federal agencies and does not by itself repeal state laws.

sections.skill: Compare changing AI rules with a sports schedule during a storm season

questions.prompt: Why might last month's printed schedule be wrong?

choices.text: Because printed schedules always contain mistakes made on purpose by the team
Games were postponed, moved or cancelled

questions.intro: During storm season, a team's schedule changes often: games are POSTPONED, MOVED to new dates, or CANCELLED, and a printed schedule from last month may be wrong. questions.prompt: Why can a summary of AI rules be out of date within months?

choices.text: Because summaries are always written incorrectly by people who never read the laws

questions.intro: Because AI rules are changing, a summary can be out of date within months. Use official sources, such as the state legislature's website, and look at the date of any secondary summary. Pay attention to the difference between "signed," "in effect," "delayed," "challenged in court" and "repealed." This course records a checked date and review interval for each such claim so readers know how fresh it is.
